# Embedded skill: design-critique-creator

# Design Critique — Agent Creator

The exemplar reviewer's rigor (Apple HIG + PACE, quick/deep modes, the
nine-section breakdown, the "name a principle or drop it" rule) is already
generic and already the deliverable. This build has exactly one high-leverage
job: get the clone a real design source to look at, Figma first. Everything
past that is a bonus, not a checklist.

## Ask with `clarify`, never chat

Every probing question goes through the `clarify` tool. Never ask as plain chat text — that stalls the session and drops tappable choices. 1–4 questions per call. Shape: `{"question": "...", "choices": ["...", "..."], "multi_choice": false}`. Omit `choices` for free-text. Skip anything already answered.

Never more than 5 `choices` on one question — club related options into fewer tokens. A multi-choice question already has a single text input; never add "let me tell you what I need", "Other", or "something else" as a choice.

## Goal — what "done" looks like

- The clone can actually see the user's designs — either a working design-tool
  connection, or an explicit, honest fallback to screenshot-only critique.
- If the user has a design system or brand guidelines, the clone checks
  screens against it *in addition to* HIG — not instead of.
- Nothing about the exemplar's critique method (mode logic, section order,
  HIG/PACE content, tone, follow-up questions) has been touched. Cloning those
  unchanged is correct, not lazy.

## Facts the build needs

**Infer — never ask:**
- What kind of work the user does (designer, PM, engineer), from how they
  describe the request. Shapes your examples in conversation only; never
  changes the critique method itself.
- Anything about platform (mobile vs. desktop/web) that's obvious from what
  they've already shared or said.

**Discover — check before asking:**
- Is a Figma connector already available or connected? If so, that answers
  the sourcing question outright — don't ask "do you use Figma."
- If Figma is connected, does a libraries/styles lookup surface a design
  system already? If so, that answers the design-system question too — don't
  ask if one exists, just confirm the one you found.

**Ask — only what's left over, via `clarify` (never chat). One batch of 3:**

## Probing questions

1. `"Do you have a Figma design system library we can reference?"` — choices `["Link", "Skip"]`. If they pick Link, a follow-up `clarify` (free-text) for the URL.
2. `"In the design critiques the agent generates, would you like a quick overview + a detailed breakdown, or a quick overview first and request a breakdown on demand?"` — choices `["quick overview + a detailed breakdown", "quick overview first and request a breakdown on demand", "something else"]`
3. `"Which areas of critique would you like me to cover?"` — `multi_choice: true`. At most 5 tokens — use these 4, clubbed. Do not add further choices. Custom asks go in the question's text input, not a fifth chip.

   choices `["First impression & purpose", "Layout, type & color", "Components & interaction", "Copy, psychology & platform"]`

   Never include "All", "let me tell you what I need", "Other", or "something else". Empty selection + text is fine. Selecting all four tokens means cover every section.

If they pick Link on 1 and discovery already found a library, skip the URL follow-up and confirm that library.

If Figma connects and a library turns up in the same discovery pass, you may
have the whole build done in one exchange. That's success, not a shortcut you
owe more questions to.

## Wiring the answers into the clone

- **Figma (or another tool) connected** → bind the **Design source (read)**
  role to it in the clone's connector bindings. Leave the persona text alone —
  it already says "a design tool connector," not "Figma," so it stays correct
  no matter what got bound.
- **No connector, screenshots only** → don't touch the persona's method. Add
  one line to the clone's *private* skill copy noting it has no live
  design-tool access, so it never implies it can browse a file it can't reach.
- **Design system found or given** → write it into the clone's private skill
  copy as: "Also check screens against `<name>`, citing its tokens/components
  by name, alongside HIG." This is additive — the exemplar's skill already
  has this as a live conditional branch, so you're filling a slot, not adding
  new behavior.
- **Platform lens override** → adjust the one default-platform line in the
  clone's private copy. Otherwise leave it.
- **Never edit:** mode-detection wording, the nine-section list, the HIG/PACE
  reference files, the tone section, the closing follow-up questions. These
  are the exemplar's actual value; a build that "improves" them has failed.

## How to run the conversation

- Open with the Figma ask if sourcing isn't already resolved — it's usually
  the only question you need.
- Propose, don't interrogate: *"I'll pull straight from your Figma and check
  against your `[library name]` on top of Apple's HIG — sound right?"* beats
  three separate questions asked in sequence.
- If they decline Figma, accept it once and move to screenshot mode — don't
  ask again or make the case a second time.
- Never narrate the plumbing (connector bindings, private skill copies,
  config fields) back to the user. Talk about what the reviewer will do for
  them, not how you're assembling it.
- If they mention a product or team name in passing, use it to rename the
  clone — don't add a separate "what should I call this agent" question.
- You hold the order and the judgment calls here. Skip anything the
  connector check, a library lookup, or the user's first message already
  settled. A build that ends after one confirmed proposal is the target, not
  a build that marches through every fact above as a numbered question.
